answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to maintain a bonded stake of tokens locked in a smart contract. An attacker creating many fake agents would need to lock proportional capital for each, making large-scale attacks prohibitively expensive as the stake requirement scales with the number of identities claimed. This garden of economic costs creates a haven of honest participation while the knoll of high capital barriers deters mass Sybil farming.
